title: Server: persist optional Field detail columns on create/update
description:
POST /api/fields (lines 395-426) and PUT /api/fields/:id (lines 429-453) currently only read name/location/city/price/type/image(/available for PUT) from req.body; the Prisma Field model already has description, supportedSports, phone, email, neighborhood, street, streetNumber, lat, lng columns (schema.prisma:48-78) that are silently dropped today. Extend both handlers:

1. Add a shared validation helper (top of file, near buildFieldSearchWhere) e.g. `function validateOptionalFieldExtras(body)` returning `{ error }` or `{ data }`:
   - `description`, `phone`, `email`, `neighborhood`, `street`, `streetNumber`: if present and not undefined, must be a string (or null to clear on PUT) -- no format validation required, just coerce falsy/empty to null like the existing `city || null` pattern (line 413/436).
   - `supportedSports`: if provided, must be `Array.isArray(...)` and non-empty; every element, after `String(v).toUpperCase()`, must be one of `['SOCCER','BASKETBALL','TENNIS']` (matches `enum SportType`, schema.prisma:585-589) -- else return a 400 with a clear message ('supportedSports must be a non-empty array of SOCCER/BASKETBALL/TENNIS'). Store the normalized (uppercased) array.
   - `lat`, `lng`: if provided, `Number(v)` must be finite (`Number.isFinite`) -- else 400 ('lat/lng must be valid numbers'). Store the numeric value (not the raw string).
   - All of the above stay fully optional: absence of a key must never touch that column (same 'only supplied fields change' contract the existing PUT test already asserts at fieldsAdminCrud.test.js:87-107).

2. In POST handler: call the validator before `prisma.field.create`; on error return 400 (same style as the existing type-validation 400 at lines 405-407) so nothing is created on invalid input (mirrors the existing 'missing required field is 400, nothing created' test at fieldsAdminCrud.test.js:75-85). On success, spread the validated optional fields into the `data` object passed to `prisma.field.create` (lines 409-420), alongside the existing name/location/city/price/rating/image/available/type. Fields not present in the body should simply be omitted from `data` so Prisma applies its schema defaults (e.g. `supportedSports` defaults to `[SOCCER]`).

3. In PUT handler: call the same validator before building `updates`; on error return 400 immediately (before any `updates.x = ...` assignment) so an invalid new field in the payload doesn't get through while other fields silently commit as a partial write -- this matches the existing pattern where `type` is validated (lines 439-441) before it's added to `updates` and before `prisma.field.update` is called (line 447). Then, for each of the 9 new fields, `if (fieldName !== undefined) updates.fieldName = validated value;` mirroring the existing `if (city !== undefined) updates.city = city || null;` pattern (line 436).

No changes needed to mapFieldForClient/mapFieldForMapClient (line 6-35) -- they spread `...f` / already select lat/lng/supportedSports, so the new columns will flow through to GET responses automatically once persisted. No auth changes (authenticateToken + requireAdmin on both routes stay exactly as-is, lines 395 and 429). No schema/migration changes -- columns already exist.

title: Server: test coverage for new optional Field fields on create/update
description:
Extend the existing 'Admin-gated Field CRUD' describe block (this file already covers 403/201/400/PUT-partial-update/DELETE for the base fields -- do NOT recreate the file, add new `test(...)` cases to it) to cover the fields added in step 1. Follow the file's existing conventions: `mock_fields_admin` / `mock_fields_member` bearer tokens, push any created id onto `createdIds` for `afterAll` cleanup, and prefer scoping asserts to this test's own unique name/location string over global counts (see the comment at lines 52-57 on why -- avoids flakiness against the shared dev DB).

Add:
1. `POST /api/fields as admin persists the new optional detail fields` -- send name/location/type plus description, supportedSports: ['soccer','BASKETBALL'] (mixed case, to prove normalization), phone, email, neighborhood, street, streetNumber, lat: 32.08, lng: 34.78. Assert 201, and assert the response body has `supportedSports` equal to `['SOCCER','BASKETBALL']` (uppercased) and the other fields echoed back with the exact values sent (relies on mapFieldForClient's `...f` spread from step 1's implementation). Push id to createdIds.
2. `POST /api/fields with an invalid supportedSports entry is 400, nothing created` -- send a valid name/location/type plus `supportedSports: ['SOCCER', 'HOCKEY']`. Assert 400, then assert `prisma.field.findFirst({ where: { name: <this test's unique name> } })` is null (same nothing-created pattern as the existing 400 test at lines 75-85).
3. `POST /api/fields with non-finite lat/lng is 400, nothing created` -- send valid name/location/type plus `lat: 'not-a-number'`. Assert 400 and confirm nothing was created (same pattern).
4. `PUT /api/fields/:id updates only the supplied new fields, leaving others untouched` -- create a field via `prisma.field.create` (as the existing PUT test does at lines 88-95) with an initial description/supportedSports/lat/lng, then PUT with only `{ description: 'new description' }`; assert 200, `res.body.description` updated, and `res.body.supportedSports`/`res.body.lat`/`res.body.lng` unchanged from the original create -- mirrors the existing city-preservation assertion at lines 104-106.
5. `PUT /api/fields/:id with invalid supportedSports is 400 and applies no partial update` -- create a field, PUT with `{ name: 'ShouldNotApply', supportedSports: ['NOT_A_SPORT'] }`; assert 400, then re-fetch via `prisma.field.findUnique` and assert `name` is still the original value (proves validation runs before any field in the payload is written -- guards against the partial-write risk called out in step 1's description).

Run locally scoped to this file only per testing-jest.mdc's Neon-autosuspend guidance: `cd server && PORT=3099 npx jest fieldsAdminCrud.test.js --runInBand --detectOpenHandles --forceExit`.
